statement: He was born in the Year of the Elephant.
alternatives: A minority of reports place the birth some years after the Elephant.
notes: The narration of Qays ibn Makhramah in at-Tirmidhi is graded differently by scholars; narrated here with attribution to the historians. Confirm number and grading.

statement: Surah al-Fil describes the fate of the people of the elephant.
notes: English rendering is a paraphrase of meaning.

statement: Abraha, the Abyssinian ruler of Yemen, marched on Makkah with an elephant to destroy the Ka'bah.
Abraha's men seized Abd al-Muttalib's camels; he asked for them back and said the House has a Lord who will protect it.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq via the Seerah works; narrated as a report, in indirect speech. Confirm Ar-Raheeq carries this exchange, otherwise cite Ibn Hisham.

statement: Lineage: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib ibn Hashim, of Quraysh.
notes: Al-Bukhari gives the lineage in the chapter heading on the sending of the Prophet. Confirm exact location.

statement: Allah chose Kinanah from the children of Ismail, Quraysh from Kinanah, Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and him from Banu Hashim.
His father was Abdullah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and his mother Aminah bint Wahb of Banu Zuhrah.
Abdullah died in Yathrib before his son's birth.
alternatives: Some reports say he died shortly after the birth.

statement: The Qur'an reminds him that Allah found him an orphan and gave him shelter.
He was born on a Monday, by his own statement when asked about fasting on Mondays.
notes: Direct speech. That the birth was in Makkah is undisputed.

statement: He was born in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal.
The date within Rabi' al-Awwal is disputed: the 12th is most widely known; al-Mubarakpuri gives the 9th; about 570 or 571 CE.
Reports of wonders on the night of the birth are not established and are omitted.
notes: Editorial statement. Reviewer to confirm the wording is fair to the range of scholarly grading (some individual reports are graded acceptable by some scholars).

statement: Abd al-Muttalib named him Muhammad, a name then rare among the Arabs.

notes: The hadith establishes that Thuwaybah nursed him; 'first, for a short time' is from the Seerah. Reviewer to decide whether to split the claim.

statement: He was entrusted to Halimah of Banu Sa'd and spent his first years with them.
notes: Muslim 162 places him as a child among other boys in the account of the opening of the chest; Halimah's name is from the Seerah.

statement: Townspeople sent infants to the Bedouin for health and pure Arabic.
